jesus-of-nazareth.notes:
No viewing; based on published criticism and reference records. Status moved from HOLD to GREY (reservations). Rule 2 check: the film's Catholic content is the Gospel, not the post-conciliar Church, so it does not meet hard rule 2; the Nostra Aetate framing is treated as a reservation per the brief. Nostra Aetate link: Greydanus's review says the document 'might be' the main influence (his reading); his separate article states Zeffirelli 'has long cited' it. I found no primary Zeffirelli statement (autobiography or interview) and did not cite one. Paul VI (post-conciliar) mentioned for facts only, not as approval. Cut: recommend only the complete version (DFI 382 min; releases 365–386 min depending on PAL speed and edition). Avoid the 2000 Carlton 270-min abridgement and the shorter cinema cut. The words of institution at the Last Supper were not confirmed; the record now says only 'reverently staged'. The Danish Film Institute record is used as the identity source because no BFI page was found and Screenonline refused connection. The CBCEW/Peter Malone PDF previously cited could not be read (binary PDF) and has been dropped. Editor: if the Founder treats a rewritten Judas as grave enough to exclude, this would become REJECT on gravity, not on hard rule 2.

Research outcome was GREY; overruled by the editor: REJECT: Editor ruling under the Founder's position (2026-10-11). Zeffirelli shaped the film by Nostra Aetate, and that conciliar reading is built into the drama: the invented scribe Zerah engineers the arrest and Judas becomes a well-meaning dupe, shifting the Gospel account of responsibility. This is the post-conciliar outlook applied to the Gospel itself, not a reservation a viewer can set aside.
